title: pm-dispatch lanes/skills.md: the skills sub-card is always Blocked-by the product card, but for a marked example the gates force the skills card first
body:
domain:skills#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaqHXh17Qc3C7MRAQw

Filing gate: ① documentation defect with a named producer (two rules texts that order the same two cards opposite ways), raised as `open_questions[0]` by the dev of PR #32546 (#32520, report 6814196068) and escalated by its contract review 6814405786 ③. ⛔ Not a claim; triage decides lane, grade, and whether this needs a decision card first.

## The two texts

- `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/skills.md` L12: 「子卡带 `Blocked-by:` 产品卡,技能只记已落地的行为」 — the skills sub-card always waits on the product card.
- `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md` §4 「已发布 skills」 item, as PR #32546 rewrites it: when a marked example (`os:check` TS, or a marked YAML fence) writes the retired key, `check:skill-examples` / `check:yaml-examples` turn the retirement PR red, so the skills card lands first and the retirement card is `Blocked-by:` it.

## Why the lane line has to yield in that case

Both example gates run on every PR with no paths filter (`lint.yml`), and a product-lane PR never edits `skills/**` (`lanes/skills.md` L13), so under the lane line's order the retirement PR is red with no legal repair. The lane line's reason still holds for the reversed case: a skills card that only removes a key from an example records nothing unlanded. The review recommends option A: a net-zero edit to `lanes/skills.md` naming the gate-forced exception (or pointing at the playbook's order).

## Reach

Every seat that files the skills sub-card for a spec retirement from the lane charter alone: it writes the `Blocked-by:` the wrong way round.

## Duplicate check

Searched open issues for the lane line; only #32520 names it. No open card.
